  4. A person who is a holder of national intangible cultural property recognized by the Act on the Safeguarding and Promotion of Intangible Cultural Heritage or any other person who has been under the holder's tuition for inheritance of such intangible cultural property;
  5. A person who has passed an examination prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (3) The heads of various levels of schools and lifelong educational establishments may recognize cross-credits, educational attainment or degree which learners have earned in domestic and foreign various levels of schools, lifelong educational establishments and lifelong educational institutions under Article 31.

CHAPTER VIII SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 42 (Administrative Disposition) (1) Where the founder of a lifelong educational establishment falls under any of the following, the Minister of Education or the superintendent of education may revoke his or her authorization or registration to establish such establishment or close its lifelong education courses, and order the operation of lifelong education courses to be fully or partially suspended for a fixed period not exceeding one year: Provided, That in cases of subparagraphs 1 and 4, the authorization and registration shall be revoked: <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013; Dec. 30, 2013; Mar. 27, 2015; Apr. 18, 2023>
  1. Where he or she has obtained authorization or registration or filed a report by fraud or other improper means;
  2. Where his or her establishment has fallen short of standards for authorization or registration;
  3. Where he or she has managed and operated his or her lifelong educational establishment by improper means;
  4. Where he or she falls under a cause for disqualification prescribed in any subparagraph of Article 28 (2);
  5. Where he or she fails to comply with an order for correction or changes issued under Article 34-2 (5) within a specified period without good cause;
  6. Where he or she has changed and operated his or her lifelong educational establishment without obtaining authorization for such changes, or filing for registration or report of such changes in violation of Article 38-2.
  (2) The Minister of Education or the superintendent of education may order correction or improvement regarding a violation, allowing a fixed period of at least one month, before ordering the lifelong education courses to be fully or partially suspended pursuant to paragraph (1). <Newly Inserted on Mar. 27, 2015>
  (3) Where the Minister of Education revokes authorization for a lifelong educational establishment, the graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment and degrees equal to those of graduates of a junior college or a university under paragraph (1), the head of the relevant facility shall submit to the Minister of Education, by preparing the matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as measures to protect enrolled students. <Newly Inserted on Apr. 18, 2023>

Article 42-2 (Guidance or Supervision) (1) The Minister of Education or the superintendent of education may provide guidance or supervision for a lifelong educational establishment that has obtained authorization for establishment or designation, or that has filed registration or report, in regard to matters such as accounting management and operation status.
  (2) When necessary for the guidance or supervision under paragraph (1), the Minister of Education or the superintendent of education may request the head of a relevant lifelong educational establishment to submit materials or may give other necessary instructions to the head of a relevant lifelong educational establishment, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (3) In either of the following cases, the Minister of Education and the head of a local government may require public officials under his or her jurisdiction to investigate documents, such as books, of a provider of lifelong education programs or an interested party: <Newly Inserted on Jun. 8, 2021>
  1. Where necessary for verifying the appropriateness of the issuance and use of lifelong education vouchers;
  2. Other cases prescribed by Presidential Decree as necessary for implementing lifelong education voucher projects.
  (4) A person who conducts an investigation pursuant to paragraph (4) shall carry the identification indicating his or her authority and documents stating matters prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Education, such as the period and scope of investigation, the investigator, and relevant statutes, and shall present them to the interested parties. <Newly Inserted on Jun. 8, 2021>
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Mar. 27, 2015]

Article 43 (Hearings) Where the Minister of Education or the superintendent of education intends to take any of the following measures, he or she shall hold a hearing: <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013; Mar. 27, 2015; May 29, 2016>
  1. Cancellation of the qualification of a certified lifelong education teacher prescribed in Article 24-2;
  2. Cancellation of authorization or registration prescribed in Article 42 (1).

Article 44 (Delegation and Entrustment of Authority) (1) The Minister of Education may delegate part of his or her authority under this Act to the superintendents of education, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013; May 22, 2013>
  (2) The Minister of Education may fully or partially entrust NILE with the following duties, as prescribed by Presidential Decree: <Newly Inserted on May 22, 2013; Jun. 8, 2021; Apr. 18, 2023>
  1. Training of certified lifelong education teachers under Article 24 and issuance and re-issuance of certificates for certified lifelong education teachers;
  2. Designation of training institutions for certified lifelong education teachers under Article 25.
  3. Management of issuing and using lifelong education vouchers under Articles 16-2 and 16-3;
  4. Establishment and operation of the comprehensive information system for lifelong education under Article 18-2;
  5. Management of the current status of lifelong educational establishments established by the heads of schools defined in Article 2 of the Higher Education Act pursuant to Article 30 (1).
  (3) The superintendents of education may delegate part of authority under this Act to the heads of district offices of education under their control, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Newly Inserted on May 22, 2013>
  [Title Amended on May 22, 2013]

Article 45 (Prohibition of Use of Similar Name) No one other than the Promotion Committee, NILE, the lifelong educational council, lifelong study hall, and lifelong study center, National Literacy Education Center, and City/Do literacy education center prescribed in this Act shall be allowed to use a name similar to that of such organizations. <Amended on Jan. 28, 2014; Feb. 3, 2016>

Article 45-2 (Penalty Provisions) Where a person who has established or operates a lifelong educational establishment subject to recognition of educational attainment under Article 31 (2) falls under any of the following, he or she shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than two years or by a fine not exceeding 20 million won:
  1. Where he or she violates Article 28 of the Private School Act applicable mutatis mutandis under Article 31 (8);
  2. Where he or she violates Article 29 (6) of the Private School Act applicable mutatis mutandis under Article 31 (8).
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Mar. 27, 2015]

Article 45-3 (Penalty Provisions) Any of the following persons shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than one year or by a fine not exceeding 10 million won: <Amended on Jun. 8, 2021>
  1. A person who has been issued with a lifelong education voucher or has any other person issued with such voucher, by fraud or other improper means;
  2. A person who sells or lends a lifelong education voucher or uses such voucher by improper means, in violation of Article 16-3 (3);
  3. A person who lends or borrows a certificate of qualification or recommends such acts, in violation of Article 24 (5).
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Dec. 3, 2019]

Article 46 (Administrative Fines) (1) Any of the following persons shall be subject to administrative fines not exceeding five million won: <Amended on Dec. 30, 2013; Mar. 27, 2015; Feb. 3, 2016; Mar. 23, 2021; Jun. 8, 2021>
  1. A person who has refused to provide a lifelong education program without good cause, in violation of Article 16-3 (2);
  2. A person who has failed to furnish data or furnished false data, in violation of Article 18 (2);
  3. A person who has failed to take necessary measures, such as return of study expenses, in violation of Article 28 (4);
  4. A person who has neglected to file a report under Articles 32 (5), 33 (2) and (3), 35 (2), 36 (3), 37 (3) and 38 (3);
  5. A lifelong educational establishment or the founder thereof that has violated any order issued under Article 42 (2);
  6. A person who has used a similar name, in violation of Article 45.

Any person who has completed any course in social education under previous Social Education Act at the time when this Act enters into force shall be deemed to have completed such course under this Act.
Article 12 (Transitional Measures concerning Recognition of Educational Attainment)
Any person who is recognized as having educational attainment equal to that of a graduate of a middle school or high school after having completed courses in social education under the previous Social Education Act at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed recognized as having such educational attainment after having completed courses in social education under this Act.
Article 13 (Transitional Measures concerning Specialist in Social Education)
Any person who has acquired a specialist qualification for social education under the previous Social Education Act at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed to have acquired a qualification as a lifelong education teacher under this Act.

Article 16 (Relationship with Other Statutes)
Where the previous Lifelong Education Act is cited by other statutes at the time this Act enters into force and this Act has any provisions falling under the cited provisions, this Act shall be deemed cited.
